topic: Among patients undergoing diagnostic sampling of pulmonary lesions or mediastinal lymph nodes, does rapid on-site cytologic evaluation increase the probability of an adequate sample compared with no rapid on-site evaluation?

pico.population: Patients undergoing diagnostic sampling of pulmonary lesions or mediastinal or hilar lymph nodes
pico.intervention_or_exposure: Rapid on-site cytologic evaluation during sampling
pico.comparison: No rapid on-site cytologic evaluation during sampling

targets.comparison: Rapid on-site cytologic evaluation during diagnostic sampling versus no rapid on-site evaluation
targets.population_or_subgroup: Patients undergoing diagnostic sampling of pulmonary lesions or mediastinal or hilar lymph nodes

timepoint_policy.rule: Capture source-defined adequacy assessed during or immediately after the index diagnostic sampling procedure; preserve whether the unit is patient, procedure, or specimen.

primary_analysis_spec.outcome_group: Adequate diagnostic sampling with rapid on-site evaluation
selection_rules: Select one complete binary adequate-sampling record per report when it compares rapid on-site cytologic evaluation with no rapid on-site evaluation.

Require source-defined adequate-sample counts, group denominators, and a calculator-generated RD. Where a study has multiple intervention arms, use only a contrast with the same sampling modality and needle system in both groups.
Do not use target-review forest rows, review totals, article-specific labels, or target pooled effects.
Select at most one eligible effect per independent study for this analysis.
Timepoint eligibility: Capture source-defined adequacy assessed during or immediately after the index diagnostic sampling procedure; preserve whether the unit is patient, procedure, or specimen.
outcome_terms: Adequate diagnostic sampling with rapid on-site evaluation
